title: AI great for creating level/environmental editors
author: gordonmcdowell
selftext:
Think this is fairly obvious in retrospect, but I've spent far too much time hand-editing level configurations (and using AI to focus on trying various gameplay mechanics) rather than letting AI build the tools by which levels can be edited visually.

Along those lines, I earlier learned play testing can benefit from everything on-screen having an ID, every bit of music and sound effect having an ID, and all sorts of state-of-mind monitors being displayed on-screen continually. One window is dedicated to visualizing music. (Gameplay is now 1/4 of my screen real estate.) I'm video capturing screen and often reviewing video frame-by-frame.

MacOS Golden Gate finally allows QuickTime to record both video **and audio**. (Everyone was using 3rd-party-tools until now?) I don't know who might be doing game dev on a Mac who isn't already running Golden Gate (MacOS 27), but I'd recommend using Golden Gate for that QuickTime feature alone. (I'm unaware of any downside compared to Tahoe at all.)
